record.category: file host with a permanent anonymous tier, the flagship debrid source

free_tier.stated: 'Every service is available free of charge, in a limited form' and the Visitors column names 'Advertising, captcha, waiting time, limited speed, removal after 15 days'
free_tier.notes: the four stated restrictions did not bind on the measured path: see egress and limits

per_object_cap.stated: not stated for Visitors; Premium Light 500 GB names '300 GB per file', so the paid cap is 300 GB

retention.stated: Visitors: 'removal after 15 days'; a directory file uploaded 2022-11-25 was still served on 2026-10-23, so the 15 days counts inactivity, not age
retention.notes: activity-based; the number of days between last download and deletion was not measured

egress.terms: free and unmetered by bytes: 4.36 MiB/s at 1 connection, 6.05 at 8 and 6.40 at 32, with every range honoured; 6.40 MiB/s is 5.3 TB/month of continuous transfer

record.interface_detail: https://1fichier.com/?<id> 302s straight to a node URL a-NN.1fichier.com/<token> that streams and honours Range; public folders export as JSON with ?json=1
record.tooling: rclone has no 1fichier backend; JDownloader, aria2 and a 10-line wrapper all work; the JSON folder export makes listing scriptable without an account
record.chaining: the fastest free host measured here, so it is the right cold-storage mirror for anything a debrid can also read; pair it with a rented debrid for the hosts that rate-limit

limits.value: 6.40 MiB/s aggregate at 32 connections; no connection above 8 improved on 6.05 MiB/s
Visitors are told 'removal after 15 days', so an object can disappear between sessions

record.binding_note: Nothing counts bytes on the free tier; the measured 6.40 MiB/s aggregate is the only thing between the account and 5.3 TB/month, and the paid tier exists to remove the speed limit rather than a quota.

identity_cost.detail: no account, cookie or captcha was presented: a bare GET on https://1fichier.com/?29nsorxu2te2sen8ulvq returned 200 with 35,895,659 bytes, twice in a row

record.reliability_note: The published Visitors restrictions (captcha, waiting time, limited speed) were absent at the HTTP layer on this path, and a second full download from the same IP 90 s later was served at 5.87 MiB/s; a client that trusts the vendor page will implement a queue it does not need.
record.confidence_note: Full 34.2 MiB object downloaded and hashed twice, plus two ranged concurrency runs, all in on 2026-10-23. A second IP and a file inside the 15-day inactivity window would test the retention claim.

evidence.proved: 35,895,659 bytes, sha256 15b98b4d48c14ff6256dc238826e6dc779c7575c71c281283e5450a4a425f6bb in 7,850.9 ms (4.360 MiB/s); a second full GET 90 s later 5,828.9 ms (5.873 MiB/s); 8 connections 5,654.3 ms (6.054 MiB/s); 32 connections 5,350.2 ms (6.398 MiB/s) with 32 of 32 ranges honoured
a public folder exports as JSON with filename, size and link per object, and no credential: the 35,895,659 byte RPI2DMD tutorial zip was found this way
'Every service is available free of charge, in a limited form' and the Visitors column: 'Advertising, captcha, waiting time, limited speed, removal after 15 days'

record.notes: The 41.91 MB FLAC found through MultiUp was dead (HTTP 404 on the 1fichier link), which is why the object is a 2022 zip from a public folder instead.

extras.wait_between_downloads: none observed: a second full download started 90 s after the first and ran at 5.87 MiB/s

card.summary: Unlimited hot storage; 10 TB cold storage included. Additional cold storage €1/TB/month. File cap 300 GB, unlimited file count. Retention = whole subscriptio...

free_tier.stated: Unlimited hot storage; 10 TB cold storage included. Additional cold storage €1/TB/month. File cap 300 GB, unlimited file count. Retention = whole subscription period on paid plans.

retention.stated: kept for the whole subscription period on a paid plan ('Retention: 15 days without an account, 30 days on a free account, the whole subscription period on a paid plan')

egress.terms: Verbatim, prices page: 'Premium … Unlimited downloads, with no monthly allowance'. Unlimited downloads = no egress meter at all on the plan. Plus 500 GB/month of CDN credits (Premium GOLD) valued at '€20 for 1 TB, up to €400 for 20 TB'. No per-GB egress fee anywhere on the page.

record.interface_detail: REST API (api.html), FTP upload (upload-only), rclone native backend, WebDAV via third party
record.tooling: rclone '1fichier' backend is first-class; REST API documents available_cold_storage / upload_forbidden so quota is machine-readable
record.chaining: AList/OpenList mount; FTP ingest; API copy of an existing 1fichier link is instant and uses zero bandwidth (documented: 'The copy is instant and uses no bandwidth, neither yours nor ours')
record.limits_note: 300 GB/file; web upload 500 files and 500 GB per upload / 4 h max; cold/hot classification means a file >60 days undownloaded migrates to the cold bucket; Premium = 1 public IP at a time

identity_cost.detail: registration asks only for an email address, a password and an image confirmation code, with no phone; payment by bank transfer, cryptocurrency, credit card or virtual currency, so no card is needed; paid plans do not renew automatically

record.reliability_note: Cold-storage overflow is destructive: forum reports say exceeding the cold quota earns a notice that the surplus is erased in 14 days and the account is blocked. Treat cold quota as a hard wall, not a soft one.
record.confidence_note: the prices page, help page, registration form and API page were read on 2026-10-30; the record states what they say

record.provider: 1fichier — registered free account, 5 TB of temporary storage with FTP + API

free_tier.stated: Registered (free) tier: '5 TB of temporary storage', folder sharing, remote upload, FTP upload and API access; files kept 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access. Paid ladder, 1-year list prices: Premium Light 500 GB EUR 10, Premium Light 1000 GB EUR 20, Premium EUR 60 with 4 TB cold storage, Premium GOLD EUR 120 with 10 TB cold storage; sale prices until November 2: Premium EUR 30, Premium GOLD EUR 50.

per_object_cap.stated: up to 300 GB per file, as the help page's limits list and the home page state; the prices page lists '300 GB per file' among the Premium Light additions, so a lower cap on free accounts is unverified

retention.stated: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access; a qualified access is a real view or download, and automated calls do not count

egress.terms: Downloads are unlimited on the free tier but ad/wait-gated and speed-limited, with a human-verification step; Premium removes ads and gives 300 GB per file and unlimited speed. Free-tier egress is 'unmetered but shaped'. The shaping, not the bytes, is the limit.

record.tooling: Documented REST API, open to every registered account; download tokens and FTP sub-accounts are reserved to paid plans, and requests are limited to 3 per second. FTP upload and remote upload (URL pull) on free accounts. rclone ships a 1fichier backend, whose documentation says a Premium subscription is required to use it.
record.chaining: Free accounts need only an email address, so the up-to-5 TB of temporary storage is per account; every file still expires 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access.

limits.value: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access

record.limits_note: Files expire 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access. Up to 300 GB per file per the help page; web upload 500 files and 500 GB per upload, 4 hours maximum. The 5 TB is 'temporary storage'.

identity_cost.detail: registration asks only for an email address, a password and an image confirmation code; no phone and no card

record.reliability_note: 1fichier/DStorage is a carrier with its own transit, so egress is not a marginal cost for them. Which is why the free 5 TB survives where others died. The 30/90-day retention clock is the practical failure mode: it is a staging area, not an archive.
record.confidence_note: the prices page, help page, registration form and API page were read on 2026-10-30; the record states what they say
